column12: launched at 1435 with the Ryujo as its objective ... originally 30 dive bombers and 8 torpedo planes; Ryujo, a heavy cruiser and three destroyers 'bearing 317 T., distance 198 miles from our force' (Enterprise scouts, 1440)

Saratoga was about 5-8 mi from Enterprise (ONI says carriers about 5 miles apart; Cv6 report says Saratoga 10-15 mi on disengaged side later). Ryujo was steering SW at ~30 kn toward the US force (closing). Strike found Ryujo only at 1606 at 06-30S 160-45E (after chasing a second sighting 75 mi NE of Ryujo), attack began 1620, i.e. about 91 min to find it. One SBD and one TBF turned back mechanical. Groups recovered Saratoga ~1845 and after sunset; 'Not a pilot, crewman, or plane of the Saratoga attack group was lost'. Return carrier position not stated. No fuel loss.

Idea of striking Ryujo earlier was abandoned for fear planes 'would not be able to return before nightfall' (doctrine.md). 7 F4F stayed as CAP. Planes flew on 'following instructions' to Henderson Field (all but one TBF) and spent the night there: 36 landed ashore. Why ashore: ONI says only 'following instructions'; inferred reason: the convoy was a search target far from the carrier and recovery on return was not expected (not stated). Next morning the group, minus two SBD forced back to the island field, rejoined Saratoga about 1130 (deferred rendezvous 0800 -> 1100).

Report uses 'zone plus 10' clock and writes the launch time as '090'; ONI shows 0700 (different zone, not converted). OUTCOMES: no Hornet fighter returned to the ship: they stayed with the SBD until forced to head for Midway for lack of gas; 5 pilots rescued (ONI: 8). 13 SBD of Bombing 8 landed at Midway for lack of gas, 2 in the lagoon out of gas; 11 gassed and returned to Hornet 1727. Scouting 8 and Bombing 8 never found the enemy. 15 TBDs (Waldron) found it and were lost to combat.

column12: Beginning at 0830, the Hornet launched two waves ... first ... 15 SBD-3's ... 6 TBF-1's ... and 8 F4F-4's ... ordered launched to strike the Shokaku ... steaming about 210 miles to the northwest of Task Force KING
column14: https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USN/USN-CN-SantaCruz/USN-CN-SantaCruz-6.html (Our attack groups, p.51)
column19: RANGE AS STATED for the carriers' reported position (naval miles taken as nautical). Dive bombers sighted heavy cruisers 'about 150 miles out' at 1015; the carriers had moved on and were never found. CLOSING/OPENING: Japanese carriers were retiring NW. RETURN: Hornet was already dead in the water when the planes returned (1155) and they went to Enterprise. FUEL (see outcomes): 2 TBF water landings out of fuel and 1 TBF missing.

column12: The second Hornet wave, which began taking off at 0915, was made up of 9 SBD-3's and 9 TBF-1's, with 7 F4F-4's ... 'At 160 miles out an enemy DD was sighted'
column14: https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USN/USN-CN-SantaCruz/USN-CN-SantaCruz-6.html (Second Hornet wave, p.52-53)
column19: Same 210-mile carrier position as the first wave (stated for the first). Reached the end of its leg at about 160 miles, saw only cruisers/destroyers, attacked Chikuma and a Tone-class cruiser at 1040. Returned to a crippled Hornet and landed on Enterprise: the 9 SBD all aboard by about 1330; of the TBF flight 'the remaining three made water landings after exhausting their fuel'.

column12: at 0900, the Enterprise began launching 3 SBD-3's of Bombing Squadron TEN, 8 TBF-1's ... and 8 F4F-4's of Fighting Squadron TEN
column14: https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USN/USN-CN-SantaCruz/USN-CN-SantaCruz-6.html (p.51; another page of the same narrative says launched 0847)
column19: Range inferred as the same 210-mile target as the Hornet waves (ONI gives it for the group). The TBF leader asked the fighters if they could fly 90 miles farther to the reported carriers; the fighter leader (Flatley) 'having exhausted excessive fuel in combat, replied in the negative' (doctrine.md). Of the TBFs 4 survived the attack; 2 landed on Enterprise 1425, 2 ran out of gas over the force and made water landings.
